entries.english: (Co-)plaintiff/applicant/intervenor: Eitel Wilhelm von Crailsheim zu Erkenbrechtshausen (defendant at first instance). (Co-)defendant/intervenor: Thomas Aigner zu Crailsheim and Georg Hornung, under-bailiff of Ansbach, as Brandenburg margrave's counsel (plaintiff or interested party at first instance), as well as Margrave Georg Friedrich of Brandenburg-Ansbach and Brandenburg-Kulmbach as interested parties. Plaintiff's procurators: Dr. Michael Mack (1555); Dr. Julius Mart (1555). Defendant's procurators: Lic. Mauritius Breunle (1549); Lic. Martin Reichardt (1556). Subject of dispute (contemporary): appeal. Subject of dispute (modern): dispute over the jurisdiction of the regional court of the Burgraviate of Nuremberg. Subject at first instance: At the end of May 1554, Thomas Aigner brought various claims against the plaintiff before the imperial regional court of the Burgraviate of Nuremberg: 300 florins plus interest on a loan granted around St George's Day 1550; 10 florins in service pay; two garments and a pair of boots annually under an employment relationship existing since Michaelmas 1549, of which he had received only three winter garments; for 1553, additionally 1 ( shock of straw, 3 ( cords of wood, ( malter of spelt, and 1 malter of oats; just under 12 florins from a bequest by the plaintiff's brother Heinrich von Crailsheim; and about 11 further florins in advances. Invoking an exemption privilege obtained from Emperor Charles V in mid-March 1548, the plaintiff raised declinatory pleas, which Georg Hornung, Brandenburg margrave's counsel, rejected. In mid-January 1555 the regional court declared the pleas inadmissible and ordered the plaintiff to answer. The plaintiff appealed, asserting that under the imperial privilege he was exempt from the regional court's jurisdiction; that Erkenbrechtshausen was enrolled in the Odenwald knightly canton and lay near the two margravial administrative seats of Crailsheim and Werdeck, recently acquired from the landgravial Leuchtenberg and comital Hohenlohe possessions, and thus outside the regional court's district. The interested party referred to the much older privilege of the imperial regional court, whose jurisdiction had always extended to members of the Altmühl and Odenwald knightly cantons. The defendant pleaded that the time limit had been missed. Proceedings: 1. Imperial regional court of the Burgraviate of Nuremberg at Ansbach, 1554. 2. Imperial Chamber Court, 1555 (1565). Invitations and reports to Eitel Wilhelm von Crailsheim concerning meetings of the Odenwald canton of knights, 1543 (1554) (Q 21–25); letter from King Ferdinand I concerning the calling of a meeting of the Franconian knighthood, 1554 (Q 26); enfeoffment charter of King Rudolf I for Burgrave Friedrich III of Nuremberg, 1273, authenticated by Abbot Friedrich V of Langheim in 1560 (Q 29); privileges of Kings and Emperors Sigismund (1417), Friedrich III (1456), and Charles V (1521) concerning the regional court of the Burgraviate of Nuremberg, each authenticated by Abbot Johann V of Langheim in 1528 (Q 30–32); prior file (Q 34) contains Charles V's exemption privilege for Eitel Wilhelm von Crailsheim, 1548; excerpts from records of Imperial Chamber Court proceedings: Eitel Wilhelm von Crailsheim against Thomas Aigner; mayor and council of the imperial city of Rothenburg ob der Tauber against Zaisolph von Rosenberg; Wilhelm von Breidenbach against the communities of Unkel and Breidenbach; and (Georg and Moritz) von Linstow against (Andreas and Christoph) von Flotow. Notes: register, start of proceedings 1555. Previous instance: Nuremberg, Burgraviate; regional court under Brandenburg control (seat: Ansbach; formerly also Cadolzburg, Fürth, and Neustadt an der Aisch).
